newsitem.title: GERMANY: SKI JUMPING-TEENAGER PETERKA STRETCHES WORLD CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-TEENAGER PETERKA STRETCHES WORLD CUP LEAD.

text.p: Slovenian teenager Primoz Peterka stretched his lead at the top of the ski jumping World Cup standings with a towering win at the New Year event in Garmisch-Partenkirchen on Wednesday.
Peterka, 17, produced jumps of 117.5 and 118.0 metres to put him well clear of the day's next best distance of 115.5 metres, achieved by Germany's Dieter Thoma and Takanobu Okabe of Japan.
The jumps gave him a total of 241.9 points. Austria's World Cup champion Andreas Goldberger, produced two 114.0 metre leaps to earn 228.9 points, and Okabe came third with 226.7.
Peterka's win, in the second event of the Four Hills Tournament, put him on 492 points in the World Cup standings after eight events, ahead of Goldberger on 432 and Norway's Kristian Brenden on 427.
Thoma, who won last Sunday's event in Oberstdorf, recovered from 16th place after his first jump to finish eighth.
